findings.title: `tape_complete_through` is described as the newest stored trade, which the schema comment explicitly says it is not
findings.description:
The field description reads "Created time of the newest stored trade", and `serve_timeseries.tape_facts` repeats it at `src/manta_trading/data/kalshi/serve_timeseries.py:124` ("The trades tape's floor and its newest stored trade"). The value actually assigned is `sync_state.watermark_ts` (`serve_timeseries.py:141-144`), whose semantics the migration states twice and emphatically: `src/manta_trading/schema/migrations/kalshi.py` (kalshi_007) — "trades: the tape is complete through this instant (end of the last fully walked window) - **NOT the newest stored trade** (slice 265, Decision 1)". `trade_status.TradeStatus.tape_through` carries the same wording.

This is not pedantry: the two differ whenever a window is walked with no trades in it, and the difference is exactly what a client uses the field for (deciding whether an empty window is a gap or a quiet market) — which is the stated purpose of the D5 facts. The docstrings reintroduce the confusion 265 D1 was written to remove. Note the impact is confined to the source: I confirmed these routes declare `response_class=Response` with no response model, so `docs/api/openapi.json` shows `200` with no content schema and none of these `Field` descriptions reach the published artifact.

findings.title: `_admit_rows` and `_not_found` are duplicated across the two Kalshi route modules
findings.description:
`kalshi_catalog.py:81-95` and `kalshi_timeseries.py:66-79` are the same function: same 422 status, same "the request matches {count:,} rows, over the {max_rows:,} row limit; …" message, differing only in the trailing remediation phrase ("narrow the filter" vs "narrow start/end"). `_not_found` is likewise duplicated — `kalshi_catalog.py:97` already takes a `resource` argument, while `kalshi_timeseries.py:59` hardcodes `"Market"`.

This is the same argument the new `routes/windows.py` docstring makes for extracting the day-boundary convention ("two derivations of 'the last instant of a day' is exactly how one of them ends up exclusive by accident"), and AGENTS.md forbids duplicated logic. The two remediation phrases are the only genuine difference, so a single helper parameterized by that phrase (the pattern `_not_found(resource, ticker)` already demonstrates) collapses them without losing the tailored message. The reversed-range 422 text is a third copy: `bars.py:97` and `windows.py:62` render byte-identical strings.

findings.title: `TradeRecord.from_row` unpacks positionally, unlike the mapping-driven candle path
findings.description:
`CandleRecord.from_row` walks `CANDLE_COLUMNS` so that, per the module docstring, "a column added there is served here without an edit". `TradeRecord.from_row` instead indexes `values[0]`…`values[7]`, restating `TRADE_VALUE_COLUMNS` order by position. A column inserted anywhere but the end of `trade_repository.TRADE_COLUMNS` shifts every later index and silently assigns the wrong value to the wrong field — silently because the types line up (`taker_book_side` is `str | None` just like `trade_id`'s `str` after `str()`, and every price column is `Decimal`). The one test that touches the mapping, `test_value_count_matches_the_repository_mapping` in `test/integration/test_kalshi_serving.py`, asserts only `len(r.values) == len(TRADE_COLUMNS) - 1`, which a shift preserves.

The `strict=True` zip in the candle path would raise on an arity change; the positional path would not. Driving the trade record from the same mapping (or at least zipping `TRADE_VALUE_COLUMNS` against `row.values`) would make the two `from_row` implementations one design instead of two.

findings.title: `_window`'s `extra` argument both merges parameters and decides which predicate is emitted
findings.description:
`extra` is documented as extra *params* (`params: dict[str, Any] = {"ticker": ticker, **(extra or {})}`), but at lines 198-199 its mere truthiness appends `period = %(period)s`. The coupling is only correct because the single caller (`_candle_window`) happens to pass exactly `{"period": period}`. A future caller passing `extra` for any other reason gets a `period` predicate referencing an unbound parameter and a psycopg error at query time — a failure far from the line that caused it.

An explicit `period: int | None = None` parameter, with the clause emitted from that, makes the two roles separate and the constraint visible in the signature. `count_candles`/`fetch_candles` would pass it; `count_trades`/`fetch_trades` would not.

findings.title: `CANDLES_CEILING_RESPONSE_MB` is defined and never read
findings.description: The constant records the D8 open question's measurement, but nothing references it — `test_candles_at_the_admission_ceiling_records_its_response_size` recomputes `megabytes` from `len(response.content)` and hardcodes "186 measured 11.58 MB for bars" in the printed line, while `CANDLES_CEILING_RESPONSE_MB` sits unread. So the test that exists to record the figure cannot notice the figure changing; its own docstring's claim that the measurement is "recorded here" is not true of any executable assertion. Either assert the constant against the measurement (which is what makes it a recording rather than a comment) or drop the constant and keep the printed value.

findings.title: `CandleRow` says fourteen value columns; `values` holds sixteen
findings.description: The docstring reads "its period end plus the fourteen value columns", but `CANDLE_VALUE_COLUMNS` is `tuple(name for name, _ in CANDLE_COLUMNS)`, and `CANDLE_COLUMNS` is 4 (`yes_bid`) + 4 (`yes_ask`) + 6 (`price`) + `volume_fp` + `open_interest_fp` = 16. Fourteen is the count of columns that get *re-nested* (the model module's "the fourteen flat stored columns are re-nested" is defensible for that reason), but it is not the length of `values`. This slice's own load test says sixteen ("a candle carries sixteen decimal strings where a bar carries five floats", `test_188_kalshi_api_nfr.py:334`), and the constant's docstring in `constants.py` says sixteen. Since `from_row` zips this tuple against `CANDLE_COLUMNS` with `strict=True`, the length is load-bearing and the comment should match it.

structured_findings.summary: `tape_complete_through` is described as the newest stored trade, which the schema comment explicitly says it is not
`_admit_rows` and `_not_found` are duplicated across the two Kalshi route modules
`TradeRecord.from_row` unpacks positionally, unlike the mapping-driven candle path
`_window`'s `extra` argument both merges parameters and decides which predicate is emitted
`CandleRow` says fourteen value columns; `values` holds sixteen
